Markets react as Middle East conflict flares up.
Evidence: oil at $90, military strikes, stock dip
#Aletheia #Economy

Geopolitical conflict drives oil prices to $90 and pushes major stock indexes downward.

Kinetic escalation directly disrupts global energy supply chains and depresses equities.

- Washington Times: PASS (-0.7, -0.8) — Accurate market and conflict reporting.
Renewed military clashes between U.S. forces and Iranian assets in the Persian Gulf sent oil prices surging and stock markets lower.

The Bright Side:
Exposes the fragile dependence of global markets on secure maritime trade choke points.

The Breakdown & Plane Error:
Confuses tactical military posturing with sustainable economic leverage.

Escalating kinetic force to exert economic pressure creates cascading instability, forcing civilian markets to absorb the cost of geopolitical brinkmanship.

The Trajectory: The Path of Destruction.
When you map the gap between stated intentions and ground-level results, it plots a direct trajectory toward Destruction. Unchecked military escalation reliably contracts global stability.

The Unavoidable Truth: Maritime disruptions in key energy corridors immediately impact global fuel prices.

The Unavoidable Lie: Economic coercion through military strikes yields stable long-term diplomatic outcomes.
